narrativeReportMd:
# Subscription R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R6 keeps the `Subscription` canonical but redesigns the resource around `SubscriptionTopic`, structured filters, top-level channel fields, and separate status/error reporting. Hard R4→R6 instance breaks are present: ordinary R4 instances contain required `criteria` and `channel` elements that R6 does not define, and they lack required R6 `topic` and `channelType`.

## Scope
The analysis used the local R4 and R6 core package StructureDefinitions, package indexes, package metadata, selected local Subscription terminology resources, and the R6 `SubscriptionTopic`/`SubscriptionStatus` StructureDefinitions where needed to understand split responsibilities. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
The main migration problem is not a field-by-field rename. R4 subscriptions are inline search-trigger rules; R6 subscriptions point at topic definitions and carry structured filters. Channel data is flattened and typed differently, payload semantics are split into format and content level, and operational errors move away from `Subscription.error`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `Subscription:ELEMENT_PRESENCE_OR_IDENTITY:criteria-topic:7f3a1d` and `Subscription:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:channel-channelType:8b2c6e`, because they affect essentially all valid R4 Subscription instances. Payload and header conversions are also high-risk when populated because they affect PHI disclosure, authentication, and notification delivery.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is required for criteria-to-topic mapping, channel terminology/system selection, payload content policy, header/parameter parsing, and any conversion of operational errors to `SubscriptionStatus`.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Many changes appear justified by a more rigorous R6 subscription framework, but compatibility would have been improved by deprecated aliases, standard cross-version extensions, or a normative StructureMap for common R4 patterns.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `SubscriptionTopic`, `SubscriptionStatus`, Subscription operations/search parameters, and the relevant terminology expansions before finalizing a production migration plan.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `Subscription` is a major local redesign with hard R4→R6 validation breaks. The top concerns are required `criteria`/`channel` removal with new required `topic`/`channelType`, non-trivial criteria-to-topic/filter migration, and payload/header/status semantics that affect runtime delivery. The main uncertainty is the lack of official cross-version mapping and full terminology expansion for all related value sets.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a redesign exercise: map R4 criteria to `SubscriptionTopic` plus `filterBy`, flatten and retype channel settings, decide payload content policies, convert headers to structured parameters, and plan where operational status/error state lives. Reverse R6→R4 conversion is lossy for topic, structured filters, `Coding` channel types, id-only payloads, new status code `entered-in-error`, optional R6 management fields, and R6 instances omitting `reason`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural, cardinality, datatype, binding-reference, and local CodeSystem differences because both StructureDefinitions and local terminology files were inspected. Confidence is medium for intended migration semantics and exact channel-type code equivalence because official diffs, narrative migration guidance, live terminology expansions, and Subscription-specific cross-version maps were not available locally.

findings.title: Inline R4 criteria was replaced by a mandatory SubscriptionTopic reference and topic-scoped filters

oldState.summary: R4 requires Subscription.criteria as a 1..1 string containing search criteria.

semanticText.definition: The rules that the server should use to determine when to generate notifications for this subscription.
semanticText.comment: The rules are search criteria (without the [base] part). Like Bundle.entry.request.url, it has no leading '/'.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, every `Subscription` carries its own inline search criteria string in `Subscription.criteria`.

newState.summary: R6 removes criteria, requires Subscription.topic 1..1, and adds optional repeatable filterBy components tied to the referenced SubscriptionTopic.

semanticText.short: Reference to the subscription topic being subscribed to
semanticText.definition: The reference to the subscription topic to be notified about.

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the triggering definition is externalized to `SubscriptionTopic`; `Subscription.filterBy` can then narrow that topic-defined stream. There is no native `criteria` element.

facts.note: R4's required inline search expression is not present in the R6 Subscription snapshot.
R6 requires a canonical reference to a SubscriptionTopic.
R6 filter criteria are structured and tied to SubscriptionTopic.canFilterBy definitions.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 root definition describes a server checking resources against `criteria`; the R6 root definition describes a client's request to be notified about a `SubscriptionTopic`. The new `topic` and `filterBy` elements are the local R6 replacement pattern for the removed `criteria` element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and model break. A normal R4 `Subscription` must contain `criteria` and cannot contain `topic`; an R6 `Subscription` must contain `topic` and has no `criteria` element. R4 search strings also are not mechanically equivalent to R6 topic-filter definitions without knowing the target topic's allowed resources, filter parameters, comparators, modifiers, and event model.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Subscriptions are operational routing rules. An incorrect topic or filter migration can suppress expected notifications or send notifications to the wrong endpoint.

justification.inferredGoal: Move subscriptions from ad hoc inline search criteria to reusable topic definitions with constrained subscriber filters.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Allow a deprecated R4 `criteria` element as an alternative to `topic`/`filterBy` during a base R6 transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: reusable `SubscriptionTopic` definitions and topic-scoped filters make subscription behavior more computable than arbitrary inline R4 search criteria. Accomplishing that by removing `criteria` is probably justified because keeping arbitrary criteria as equal base semantics would materially weaken the conformance model and leave servers with two different trigger languages to support.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained `Subscription.criteria` as deprecated and allowed either `criteria` or `topic` for a transition, with `topic` preferred for new R6 subscriptions. That would preserve old instances for this part of the model, but it is only a partial alternative: criteria strings can be server-specific, may not map to any `SubscriptionTopic.canFilterBy`, and the deprecated representation might never disappear.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve many R4 criteria instances but would keep arbitrary search-string triggers beside the new topic model and risk indefinite duplicate trigger representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Subscription.criteria` as 1..1 string.
R6 defines `Subscription.topic` as 1..1 canonical targeting SubscriptionTopic.
evidence.quote: Reference to the subscription topic being subscribed to

evidence.detail: R6 adds repeatable `filterBy` to narrow the topic stream.
evidence.quote: Criteria for narrowing the subscription topic stream

evidence.detail: The R6 root definition describes notification based on a SubscriptionTopic.
evidence.quote: The subscription resource describes a particular client's request to be notified about a SubscriptionTopic.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.reason: Notify the care manager about new observations

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative rather than complete conformance examples. They isolate the old `criteria` pattern and the new topic/filter pattern.

findings.narrativeMd: The central local change is that R4 subscriptions were self-contained search-trigger rules, while R6 subscriptions subscribe to an externally defined `SubscriptionTopic`. This is not a simple rename: a migration needs a topic catalog and rules for translating each R4 search expression into topic-specific filters or events. Existing R4 instances will fail strict R6 validation because `criteria` is unknown and the mandatory `topic` is absent.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: a valid R4 instance with `criteria` and no `topic` is invalid against the R6 StructureDefinition. R6→R4: a valid R6 instance with `topic` and structured `filterBy` has no native R4 representation except by synthesizing a R4 `criteria` string or preserving data in extensions. Strict parsers, generated classes, and FHIRPath expressions that read `Subscription.criteria` must be rewritten.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 criteria strings, classify them by intended event/topic, and map each to an R6 `SubscriptionTopic` canonical plus zero or more `filterBy` rows. Do not assume this is lossless: criteria using unsupported parameters, chained/reverse-chained search, custom search parameters, or server-specific semantics require manual review or topic-specific extensions. Keep the original R4 criteria in an audit extension during migration if reversibility matters.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The design goal appears to require a stronger shared topic model, which is difficult to achieve while preserving arbitrary inline criteria as first-class R6 semantics. A deprecated compatibility element or official cross-version extension would have reduced instance breakage but would also perpetuate the ambiguity R6 is trying to remove.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Human review is needed for every production migration because the computable definitions identify the structural replacement but not the business mapping between local R4 criteria and available R6 SubscriptionTopics.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `Subscription.criteria` is a required inline search string, while R6 removes that element and requires a `Subscription.topic` canonical with optional topic-scoped filters. That is a real old-valid/new-invalid break for any R4 Subscription instance, and migration needs business knowledge about the intended event stream and available SubscriptionTopic definitions. However, the R6 target model is a coherent replacement for ad hoc inline criteria; keeping arbitrary criteria as a base alternative would force servers and validators to support two trigger models and would weaken the computable topic/filter design.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.criteria` is `1..1 string` with short `Rule for server push`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.topic` is `1..1 canonical(SubscriptionTopic)` and `Subscription.filterBy` is `0..*`.
Local map search found no Subscription-specific StructureMap/ConceptMap for criteria-to-topic conversion.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Subscription is FMM 3 and trial-use, so compatibility matters for a mature workflow, but it is not a normative/FMM 5 stability promise. The centrality of criteria raises the migration burden, while trial-use status makes a coherent redesign more acceptable.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a valid R4 instance has `criteria` and no `topic`, while a base R6 instance requires `topic` and has no `criteria`; generated APIs and criteria readers also need redesign.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could allow a deprecated `criteria` alternative to `topic`, but that is only partial and has major tradeoffs: it preserves old wire shape while retaining arbitrary search-trigger semantics beside the new SubscriptionTopic model, creating duplicate behavior and unclear server obligations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high impact and partial-alternative assessment; the break is real and central, but the alternative has enough design cost that the finding is not a clear Revisit.

findings.title: R4 channel backbone was flattened and channel.type changed from primitive code to Coding

oldState.summary: R4 requires a `Subscription.channel` backbone with required `channel.type` code and optional endpoint, payload, and header children.

binding.description: The type of method used to execute a subscription.

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 channel type is a primitive code under the `channel` backbone: `Subscription.channel.type`.

newState.summary: R6 removes `Subscription.channel` and requires top-level `Subscription.channelType` as a Coding; endpoint is also top-level.

binding.description: The type of method used to execute a subscription.

newState.narrativeMd: The channel type is now a top-level `Coding`, with the channel type value set composed from `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/subscription-channel-type`.

facts.oldValue: 1..1 code, required binding to R4 subscription-channel-type

facts.newValue: 1..1 Coding, extensible binding to R6 subscription-channel-type

facts.note: The R6 package includes the ValueSet but not the external terminology CodeSystem content.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same business concept, channel type, moved from `channel.type` to `channelType`; endpoint likewise moved from `channel.endpoint` to `endpoint`. The changed datatype and value set system make this more than a path-only rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Every valid R4 Subscription has a `channel` backbone, which is not an R6 element, and lacks the required R6 `channelType`. R6 generated models also expose a `Coding` object rather than a primitive enum/string. R6-to-R4 conversion must collapse a Coding to a primitive code and decide what to do with system/display/extensions or channel-type codes not accepted by R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapped channels can change the notification transport, producing missed notifications or disclosures through the wrong channel.

justification.inferredGoal: Make channel properties top-level and allow coded channel metadata with terminology system context.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `channel` backbone as deprecated while adding the R6 top-level `channelType` and `endpoint` fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Flattening channel data and using `Coding` for channel type fit the broader R6 subscription redesign and terminology model. The break is severe for every R4 instance, but the less-breaking base design would introduce material ambiguity because the same delivery configuration could be expressed twice and with different datatype semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have allowed the R4 `channel` backbone for legacy instances and required that systems populate either the old backbone or the new top-level fields, not contradictory values in both. This is a partial alternative rather than a clean one: validators, serializers, and servers would need no-conflict invariants and conversion precedence, and deprecated channel backbones could accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old channel shape but duplicate transport configuration and require conflict rules between primitive `channel.type` and Coding `channelType`.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Subscription.channel` as 1..1 BackboneElement.
evidence.quote: The channel on which to report matches to the criteria

evidence.detail: R4 defines `channel.type` as required primitive code.
R6 defines `channelType` as required Coding.
R6 defines top-level `endpoint` as the channel notification URL.
evidence.quote: URL where the channel sends notifications

evidence.detail: R6 channel type value set includes the terminology.hl7.org code system.

examples.examplesMd: A migration normally maps `channel.type` to `channelType.code` and `channel.endpoint` to `endpoint`; confirming the correct Coding.system requires the R6 channel-type terminology.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the R4 `channel` backbone and promotes channel information to top-level elements. This breaks JSON/XML shape, generated classes, serializers, database columns, and FHIRPath paths. The channel type also changes datatype from primitive `code` to `Coding`, so enum-based R4 code cannot simply be copied without selecting the R6 coding system.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: any untransformed R4 Subscription is invalid because `channel` is not recognized and required `channelType` is missing. R6→R4: a `Coding` with system/display/extensions or a code outside the R4 required value set cannot be losslessly represented as the primitive R4 `channel.type` code. Strict enum switches must account for the changed datatype and possible terminology system move.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Flatten `channel.type` to `channelType`, `channel.endpoint` to `endpoint`, and review channel-specific URL rules. Use the R6 channel-type code system expected by the value set. Add tests for each channel code used in production and for channels carrying display/system extensions. Preserve the original R4 channel object in an extension only if round-trip auditing is required.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new shape is probably justified by the broader R6 subscription redesign, but it could have been less disruptive with a deprecated R4-compatible backbone or an official conversion map. The tradeoff is that keeping both forms would require conflict resolution when both channel representations are present.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package did not include the external `CodeSystem-subscription-channel-type` resource, so code-system-level comparison is based on the R6 ValueSet compose and R4 local CodeSystem only.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 requires a `Subscription.channel` backbone containing a primitive `channel.type`; R6 removes the backbone and requires a top-level `channelType` `Coding`, with endpoint also promoted to a top-level field. This breaks wire shape and generated models for essentially every R4 Subscription, but the direct migration for channel type and endpoint is relatively mechanical. The R6 design also avoids a nested delivery configuration and gives channel type a terminology system, so preserving the old backbone in base R6 would create duplicate channel representations and conflict rules.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.channel` is `1..1 BackboneElement`; `Subscription.channel.type` is `1..1 code` with required subscription-channel-type binding.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.channelType` is `1..1 Coding` with extensible subscription-channel-type binding; `Subscription.endpoint` is top-level `0..1 url`.
R6 ValueSet `subscription-channel-type` includes `http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/subscription-channel-type`; R4 local CodeSystem used `http://hl7.org/fhir/subscription-channel-type` codes.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use raises concern because channel configuration is part of the ordinary Subscription workflow, but the maturity level still leaves room for a structural cleanup when the replacement is explicit and proportionate.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the required R4 `channel` object is not an R6 Subscription element and R4 instances lack required `channelType`; codegen changes from a nested primitive code to a top-level Coding.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained `channel` as deprecated while adding `channelType` and `endpoint`, but that would duplicate transport settings and require precedence rules when old and new fields disagree. The tradeoff is significant enough that this is not an obvious low-cost base alternative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing assessment that impact is high and the less-breaking alternative is only partial, though the fresh review emphasizes that much of the forward conversion is mechanical.

findings.title: Payload configuration split into contentType and content level, changing no-payload and partial-payload semantics

oldState.summary: R4 has optional `channel.payload` code for MIME type; absence means no payload.

binding.description: The mime type of an attachment. Any valid mime type is allowed.

semanticText.definition: The mime type to send the payload in - either application/fhir+xml, or application/fhir+json. If the payload is not present, then there is no payload in the notification, just a notification.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses one element both to request a MIME type and to imply that a payload should be sent. Omitting it means no payload.

newState.summary: R6 has optional `contentType` for MIME type and optional `content` code for empty, id-only, or full-resource payload content.

binding.description: Codes to represent how much resource content to send in the notification payload.

semanticText.definition: How much resource content to deliver in the notification payloads. The choices are an empty payload, only the resource id, or the full resource content.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates format (`contentType`) from content level (`content`), adding explicit `empty`, `id-only`, and `full-resource` payload choices.

facts.oldValue: 0..1 code bound to mimetypes; absence means no payload

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `contentType` preserves the MIME-type aspect of R4 `channel.payload`; `content` carries the new payload amount semantics that R4 encoded only indirectly through presence/absence.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that include `channel.payload` need structural and semantic conversion. Choosing only `contentType` may lose whether R6 should send `empty`, `id-only`, or `full-resource`; choosing only `content` may lose MIME format. Conversely, R6 `content='id-only'` is not natively representable in R4, which distinguishes no payload versus a MIME-typed payload but not an id-only payload.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Payload level directly affects data disclosure and downstream processing. Mapping `empty`, `id-only`, and `full-resource` incorrectly can either omit needed data or send more PHI than intended.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent notification payload format and payload content amount separately.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `channel.payload` or another deprecated shorthand for R4 MIME payloads while adding `contentType` and `content`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating payload format from payload amount is a reasonable R6 goal because it makes privacy- and delivery-relevant behavior explicit. The old R4 element combined MIME type with an implicit no-payload/full-payload distinction, so preserving it as first-class semantics would hide policy choices that R6 intentionally exposes.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have treated `channel.payload` as a deprecated alias for `contentType` plus a defined default `content`, such as `full-resource` when a MIME type is present and `empty` when absent. That preserves many R4 instances, but it is incomplete because R4 server behavior was not guaranteed to match those defaults, and keeping both old and new payload controls creates duplicate representations for a security-sensitive setting.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 payload settings but would encode policy assumptions about empty, id-only, and full-resource payloads and duplicate payload configuration.

evidence.detail: R4 payload is a MIME-type code; absent payload means no payload.
evidence.quote: MIME type to send, or omit for no payload

evidence.detail: R6 contentType is the MIME type.
evidence.quote: MIME type to send, or omit for no payload

evidence.detail: R6 content controls how much resource content is included.
R6 defines payload content codes empty, id-only, and full-resource.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is a common but policy-dependent interpretation of an R4 MIME payload as an R6 full-resource payload. It should not be applied blindly without checking the R4 server's notification behavior.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes payload behavior more explicit by splitting the MIME type from the amount of resource content. This is a meaningful semantic change because R4 overloaded presence of `channel.payload`: present meant a MIME-typed payload, absent meant notification only. R6 can express id-only payloads and explicit empty payloads, which have no direct R4 field.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: R4 `channel.payload` is nested under a removed backbone and therefore requires transformation. R6 validation will accept `contentType` and `content`, not `channel.payload`. R6→R4: `content=id-only` and any distinction between explicit `empty` and omitted content cannot be represented cleanly in native R4. Generated models and notification code that assume payload presence is equivalent to MIME-type presence need review.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `channel.payload` to `contentType` and set `content` by local policy, commonly `full-resource` for prior payload-bearing rest-hook subscriptions and `empty` for prior no-payload subscriptions. Test notification generation and security controls for no-payload, id-only, and full-resource modes. Preserve the original R4 payload setting if a lossless audit trail is needed.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A split is semantically cleaner, but the lack of a retained shorthand makes old instances invalid and makes policy assumptions explicit during migration. A deprecated alias plus conversion defaults would have been less disruptive but might hide important privacy choices.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 places the MIME payload choice in `channel.payload`, where the element's presence also signals that a payload should be sent. R6 moves the MIME type to top-level `contentType` and adds optional `content` codes for empty, id-only, and full-resource payloads. This requires migration work for populated R4 payloads and may need local policy when choosing an R6 content level, especially because payload content affects PHI disclosure. Still, separating format from content amount is a legitimate R6 goal, and carrying forward the old shorthand in base R6 would hide or duplicate that policy decision.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.channel.payload` is `0..1 code`, required binding to mimetypes, short `MIME type to send, or omit for no payload`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.contentType` is `0..1 code` bound to mimetypes and `Subscription.content` is `0..1 code` bound to subscription-payload-content.
R6 CodeSystem `subscription-payload-content` defines `empty`, `id-only`, and `full-resource`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means payload compatibility should not be dismissed, particularly because payloads can carry sensitive data. The same status also supports a careful redesign of ambiguous trial-use behavior.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: populated R4 `channel.payload` must move to `contentType` and may need a content-level policy; R6 `content=id-only` also creates R6-to-R4 loss because R4 has no native id-only payload mode.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated `channel.payload` alias or shorthand default could preserve many R4 payload settings, but it would duplicate a security-sensitive control and require assumptions such as mapping a MIME type to `full-resource`. Those assumptions may be wrong for some channels or deployments.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-risk assessment; the privacy-sensitive mapping burden is real, but because `content` is optional and `contentType` preserves the MIME-type aspect, the forward break is narrower than the old impact text suggests.

findings.title: Free-form channel headers became structured channel parameters with required name and value

semanticText.definition: Additional headers / information to send as part of the notification.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented channel-specific header information as repeated strings.

newState.summary: R6 replaces headers with 0..* `Subscription.parameter` backbone rows, each requiring `name` and `value` strings.

semanticText.definition: Channel-dependent information to send as part of the notification (e.g., HTTP Headers).

newState.narrativeMd: R6 parameterizes channel-specific information as structured name/value pairs rather than free-form strings.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `Subscription.parameter` definition explicitly cites HTTP headers, matching the main R4 use case for `channel.header`, but the representation changed from a string list to structured name/value rows.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that used `channel.header` need parsing and restructuring; strings that are not simple `name: value` pairs may not convert cleanly. Generated R6 classes require a backbone component with two mandatory children, and R6 summary queries will not include parameters even though R4 summary included headers.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Headers often carry authentication or routing data. A parsing mistake can break delivery or leak credentials.

justification.inferredGoal: Make channel-dependent parameters explicit and usable beyond HTTP headers.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `channel.header` strings alongside structured `parameter` name/value rows.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of structured channel parameters is reasonable because it supports validation and non-HTTP channel conventions better than a list of free-form strings. The break is probably justified because many R4 header strings need security-sensitive parsing, and treating both formats as equal base fields would preserve ambiguity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `channel.header` as a deprecated legacy field and introduced `parameter` for structured use. That would help old instances with simple `Name: value` headers, but it would not solve arbitrary non-header strings and would create two places to carry credentials or routing data, increasing conflict and leakage risk.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve simple header strings but retain ambiguous free-form sensitive data and duplicate channel-parameter representations.

evidence.detail: R4 header is repeatable string with summary=true.
evidence.quote: Additional headers / information to send as part of the notification.

evidence.detail: R6 parameter is repeatable BackboneElement for channel-dependent information.
R6 parameter.name is mandatory.
R6 parameter.value is mandatory.
evidence.quote: Value of the parameter to use or pass through

examples.examplesMd: The example is a fragment focused on header conversion. Real migrations should avoid logging or exposing actual secrets while transforming header values.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 generalizes R4 `channel.header` into a structured `parameter` list. This improves structure but is not lossless for arbitrary R4 strings unless the migration can parse each header or channel-specific parameter convention. It also changes summary behavior: R4 headers were summary elements, while R6 parameters are not.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: instances with `channel.header` are invalid unless transformed; each R6 parameter row must have both `name` and `value`. R6→R4: name/value pairs can be serialized back to strings for simple HTTP headers, but channel-specific parameters may not have a canonical R4 string format. Code that queries `_summary=true` may observe a changed result shape.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Parse only well-understood header formats, validate names against channel-specific rules, and handle credentials as secrets during migration. For non-header channel parameters, define local mapping rules or preserve values in extensions. Add tests for duplicate names because R6 notes that names are not required to be unique unless channel definitions impose restrictions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A structured parameter model is justified for validation and non-HTTP channels, but the absence of a retained string form makes old data require custom parsing. A dual model would reduce migration risk but could also preserve insecure or ambiguous header strings.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 free-form `channel.header` strings become R6 structured `parameter` rows with mandatory `name` and `value`. Instances that used headers need parsing and rewriting, and mistakes can break authentication or routing. The R6 structure is nevertheless a reasonable improvement because it makes channel parameters explicit and supports non-HTTP channel conventions better than an untyped string list.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.channel.header` is `0..* string` and summary=true.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.parameter` is `0..* BackboneElement`; `parameter.name` and `parameter.value` are both `1..1 string`.
R6 `Subscription.parameter` definition cites channel-dependent information such as HTTP headers.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use keeps compatibility relevant because headers can be operationally important, but it does not require preserving a weak free-form representation when a structured replacement has clear value.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: R4 string headers must be parsed into name/value components and R6 generated models require a backbone component; this is only an old-valid/new-invalid issue for instances that actually populate headers.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping deprecated header strings would preserve simple HTTP header values, but it would leave credentials or routing data in two possible locations and require conflict handling. That duplicate sensitive-data surface is a meaningful tradeoff.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing conclusion that this is a real migration and runtime risk with only a partial less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: Subscription.error was removed from Subscription and error reporting appears to move to SubscriptionStatus

oldState.summary: R4 has optional `Subscription.error` string on the Subscription resource.

semanticText.definition: A record of the last error that occurred when the server processed a notification.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stores the latest delivery/processing error directly on the Subscription.

newState.summary: R6 Subscription has no local `error`; R6 defines a separate SubscriptionStatus resource with repeatable CodeableConcept `error`.

semanticText.short: List of errors on the subscription

newState.narrativeMd: R6 separates operational status notification from the Subscription resource; error details are represented on `SubscriptionStatus`, not as a string field on `Subscription`.

facts.oldValue: absent in R4 core Subscription model
facts.newValue: 0..* CodeableConcept on a separate R6 resource
facts.note: Related R6 StructureDefinition was present in the package.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The names and definitions align, but the target is a separate resource and the R6 report is scoped to Subscription, so this is treated as a likely split rather than a direct same-resource rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances containing `Subscription.error` are invalid against R6 Subscription unless the information is dropped, converted to a separate `SubscriptionStatus`, or carried in an extension. R6 status/error notifications cannot be represented as a native field on R4 Subscription without flattening coded errors back to a string.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping error details can hide failed notifications and impair operational troubleshooting.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate mutable notification status/error reporting from the subscription request resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `Subscription.error` as a legacy last-error string while adding `SubscriptionStatus.error` for richer status events.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating mutable delivery status and error information from the subscription request is a reasonable R6 design goal. A less-breaking base field could preserve old instances that populated `Subscription.error`, but the tradeoff is material because status/error state is operational and can become inconsistent if represented both on the request resource and in separate status resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base alternative is not merely an extension or conversion guide: R6 could have kept an optional deprecated `Subscription.error` string for legacy last-error text while encouraging `SubscriptionStatus.error` for current status reporting. This is only partial because it preserves an older lifecycle model, cannot represent R6's repeatable coded errors, and may encourage systems to continue relying on a stale same-resource error field.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve R4 error data but risks stale or conflicting operational truth between Subscription and SubscriptionStatus.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `Subscription.error` as 0..1 string.
No `Subscription.error` element appears in the R6 Subscription snapshot.
R6 SubscriptionStatus defines repeatable error CodeableConcepts.
evidence.quote: List of errors on the subscription

examples.examplesMd: The migration example preserves text only. Mapping to coded `SubscriptionStatus.error` concepts would need a terminology policy.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 keeps a latest error note on the Subscription itself. R6 removes that field from Subscription and provides a richer `SubscriptionStatus` resource. That is a local split affecting persistence and APIs that read or update operational error state on Subscription.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: `Subscription.error` is an unknown element in R6. R6→R4: a list of coded `SubscriptionStatus.error` values cannot be represented losslessly as R4's single string without choosing a flattening policy. Systems that poll Subscriptions for last error must move to the R6 status pattern or related operations.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Before converting, decide whether historical last-error text should be discarded, preserved in an extension, or emitted as a `SubscriptionStatus` event/resource. If converting to `CodeableConcept`, define terminology mapping rules and keep original text. Update monitoring jobs and dashboards that read `Subscription.error`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Moving error state out of Subscription is consistent with a more explicit status model, but a standard cross-version extension or a deprecated last-error field would have eased migration for operational tooling.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The exact lifecycle and operation behavior of `SubscriptionStatus` was not fully analyzed because that resource is a related artifact, not the assigned artifact.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 stores a latest error note directly on `Subscription.error`; R6 has no same-resource `Subscription.error` and instead includes `SubscriptionStatus.error` as repeatable `CodeableConcept` on a separate status resource. This breaks systems that persist or poll error state on Subscription, but separating mutable delivery status from the subscription request is a defensible model. The optional R4 field is also less central than criteria or channel configuration.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.error` is `0..1 string` with short `Latest error note`.
R6 Subscription StructureDefinition contains no `Subscription.error` element.
R6 StructureDefinition `SubscriptionStatus.error` is `0..* CodeableConcept` with definition about errors when processing a notification.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use means operational tooling compatibility matters, but the affected field is optional server state and the R6 split has a plausible lifecycle rationale.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 Subscription carrying `error` is not valid as an R6 Subscription without transformation; R6-to-R4 conversion of repeatable coded errors to one string is lossy.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept a deprecated `Subscription.error` last-error string, but that would risk stale or conflicting operational truth between Subscription and SubscriptionStatus and would not represent repeatable coded errors.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment; the move appears justified but implementers need an explicit operational migration policy.

findings.title: Subscription.status required value set adds entered-in-error, widening a modifier element's code domain

oldState.summary: R4 Subscription.status is required code with codes requested, active, error, and off.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Local CodeSystem content was compared; no live terminology expansion was performed.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

newState.summary: R6 Subscription.status remains required and modifier, but the required value set includes an additional entered-in-error code.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The added code was present in the local R6 CodeSystem. The R4 and R6 binding strengths are both required.

flags.isModifierReason: This element is labelled as a modifier because it is a status element that contains status entered-in-error which means that the resource should not be treated as valid

newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds `entered-in-error`, a modifier-status value indicating the Subscription should not be treated as valid.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Existing R4 status codes remain valid in R6, so this is not an R4-to-R6 instance rejection for old values. It is still a high runtime/codegen risk because `status` is a required modifier element and generated R4 enums or exhaustive switch statements will not know the new `entered-in-error` value. A valid R6 Subscription with that status cannot be represented as a valid native R4 Subscription.status code.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misinterpreting `entered-in-error` as active or requested could cause systems to act on an invalid subscription.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Subscription status with the modifier status explicitly referenced by the element's modifier reason and common FHIR resource lifecycle semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: adding `entered-in-error` preserves all R4 status codes and does not create an R4-to-R6 instance break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added status code is consistent with modifier-status semantics and does not invalidate existing R4 `Subscription.status` values. The breakage described here is for R6 consumers or R6-to-R4 conversion, not for preserving R4-valid instances in base R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because the R4 code domain is widened rather than narrowed, backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable. ConceptMaps, extensions, or rejection policies may help R6-to-R4 down-conversion, but those are migration mitigations rather than less-breaking base R6 alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for R4-to-R6; the remaining issue is reverse-direction enum and validation handling.

evidence.detail: R4 local CodeSystem contains requested, active, error, and off.
R6 local CodeSystem adds entered-in-error.
evidence.quote: This subscription has been flagged as incorrect.

evidence.detail: R4 binding is required to ValueSet/subscription-status|4.0.1.
R6 binding is required to ValueSet/subscription-status|6.0.0-ballot4.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows the status value that is valid in R6 but outside the R4 subscription-status code system.

findings.narrativeMd: `Subscription.status` remains a required modifier element, but R6 adds the `entered-in-error` code. This does not invalidate existing R4 status values, yet it is important for systems consuming R6 because modifier status values affect whether the resource should be acted upon.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: old status codes are still in the R6 CodeSystem. R6→R4: `entered-in-error` cannot be placed in native R4 `Subscription.status` under the required binding. Runtime: generated enums, switch statements, and validation tables built for R4 must be updated and must treat `entered-in-error` as a non-actionable/error state.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Add `entered-in-error` to R6 status enums and lifecycle logic. When down-converting to R4, use an extension or reject the conversion rather than mapping silently to `off` or `error`, unless an implementation guide explicitly defines that behavior. Include tests asserting that `entered-in-error` subscriptions do not trigger notifications.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The code addition is justified by the modifier semantics. A backward-compatible R4 representation is only partially possible with extensions because the native R4 required value set cannot carry the new code.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds `entered-in-error` to the required `Subscription.status` value set while retaining all R4 status codes. This does not make any R4-valid status invalid in R6. R6 clients and down-converters must handle the new modifier status, but that is normal forward-version enum work rather than a base R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.
keyEvidence: R4 CodeSystem `subscription-status` contains `requested`, `active`, `error`, and `off`.
R6 CodeSystem `subscription-status` retains those codes and adds `entered-in-error`.
R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions both keep `Subscription.status` as `1..1 code`, required binding, modifier=true.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use calls for careful handling of modifier status codes, but because the code domain is widened rather than narrowed, it does not raise a forward compatibility concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 `entered-in-error` status has no native R4 code; there is no old-valid/new-invalid break for R4 status values.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed for the R4-to-R6 direction because old codes are preserved. Down-conversion can use extensions or rejection policies, but those are migration mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing evidence and reverse-direction warning, but disagree with treating the additive code as high-impact for R4-to-R6 compatibility.

findings.title: Subscription.reason changed from mandatory in R4 to optional in R6

oldState.narrativeMd: Every R4 Subscription needs a reason string.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 Subscriptions can omit the reason.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 breaking change because all R4-valid instances already contain `reason`. It is a down-conversion risk: an R6 Subscription without `reason` is invalid in native R4 unless a reason is synthesized or the instance is profiled/extended outside base R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid requiring a free-text reason in the base R6 resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: lowering `reason` from 1..1 to 0..1 preserves all R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Relaxing a required R4 element is not an R4-to-R6 breaking change. The R6 goal of not requiring free-text reason in every base instance is reasonable, and any compatibility concern is confined to reverse conversion when an R6 instance omits `reason`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable for the R4-to-R6 direction because every R4-valid instance already has `reason` and remains compatible with the relaxed R6 cardinality. Requiring `reason` in an R6 profile can support R4 round-trip needs, but that is not a base-design alternative to avoid R4 breakage.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: No R4-to-R6 base-design alternative is needed; R6-to-R4 round-tripping may require a profile or explicit defaulting policy.

evidence.detail: R4 min cardinality is 1.
R6 min cardinality is 0.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment omits `reason`; other R6 required fields are shown only to contextualize the omission.

findings.narrativeMd: The only cardinality weakening on a retained local element is `Subscription.reason`, which changed from required to optional. This helps R6 authors but creates a native R4 validation gap for R6 data that omits the reason.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: no old instance becomes invalid because of this cardinality change. R6→R4: missing `reason` violates R4's 1..1 cardinality. Synthesizing text such as 'unspecified' changes meaning and should be a conscious policy choice.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4→R6, carry the existing reason forward. For R6→R4, either require `reason` in an interoperability profile, reject instances without it, or populate a clearly marked implementation-specific value and preserve that defaulting decision in audit metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because the change weakens an R4 requirement, it is not an R4-to-R6 breaking change. The only compatibility issue is reverse direction, where profiles can restore the R4 requirement if needed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Subscription.reason` changes from required in R4 to optional in R6. That relaxes the base rule, so every R4-valid instance already satisfies the R6 cardinality for this path. The only concern is reverse conversion of an R6 instance that omits reason, which is not a reason to revisit the R6 base design.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.reason` is `1..1 string`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.reason` is `0..1 string`.
The element name and datatype remain `Subscription.reason` / `string`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not increase concern for a cardinality relaxation that preserves R4-valid instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can omit `reason`, which native R4 requires; there is no R4-to-R6 instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for R4-to-R6 compatibility. R6 profiles can require reason for round-trip use cases, but the base relaxation is already less restrictive than R4.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-conversion risk, but disagree that this should be considered a material R4-to-R6 impact.

findings.title: R6 adds optional metadata, ownership, and delivery-control fields with no native R4 counterparts

affectedLocation.newPath: Subscription.identifier | Subscription.name | Subscription.managingEntity | Subscription.heartbeatPeriod | Subscription.timeout | Subscription.maxCount

oldState.summary: R4 has no native elements for Subscription.identifier, name, managingEntity, heartbeatPeriod, timeout, or maxCount.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4's local Subscription surface is mostly status/contact/end/reason/criteria/error/channel.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional identifiers, human-readable name, managing entity reference, heartbeat interval, delivery timeout, and max event count.
newState.narrativeMd: These fields are optional in R6, so they do not block R4-to-R6 validation, but they carry information R4 cannot represent natively.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Optional additions do not make R4 instances invalid in R6, but R6 instances using these fields lose native data on down-conversion. Runtime systems that assume the R4 schema may drop delivery-control parameters such as heartbeat and timeout, changing observable notification behavior.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping managingEntity or delivery controls can affect who is authorized to modify the subscription and how reliably notifications are monitored.

justification.inferredGoal: Expose business identifiers, owner/manager metadata, and delivery controls in the base Subscription resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: these are optional R6 additions that do not invalidate R4 Subscription instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional identifiers, management metadata, and delivery-control fields is a backward-compatible way to add R6 capability for the R4-to-R6 direction. The reported risk is real for mixed-version stores and down-conversion, but it is not a breaking base R6 design choice for old instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking base R6 design is needed because R4 instances can simply omit these optional fields. R4 extensions can preserve the same data during down-conversion, but extension/backport strategies are migration mitigations and should not be counted as a `Yes` base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is R6-to-R4 data loss unless extensions or profiles are used; that is a round-trip mitigation issue, not an R4-to-R6 alternative.

evidence.detail: R6 adds optional repeatable Identifier.
R6 adds managingEntity Reference with a bounded target set.
R6 adds heartbeatPeriod unsignedInt.
R6 adds timeout unsignedInt.
R6 adds maxCount positiveInt.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment contains only the R6-only optional fields; each would require extension or omission in native R4.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds several optional fields that make Subscription more operationally expressive. They are not a validation break for old instances, but they matter for bidirectional bridges, persistence schemas, generated R4 clients, and systems that round-trip R6 subscriptions through an R4 store.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: no issue when these fields are absent. R6→R4: each field is non-native and would be rejected by strict R4 validators unless represented by extensions or dropped. Dropping delivery controls can change runtime notification behavior even if the resulting R4 resource validates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: If R4 round-trip is required, define extensions for each R6-only field or constrain R6 senders not to populate them. Treat `managingEntity` as authorization-relevant and delivery controls as operationally significant; do not silently discard them in production migrations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Optional additions are the least disruptive way to add capability for R4-to-R6. The remaining incompatibility is inherent to down-conversion unless cross-version extensions are standardized and adopted.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds optional fields such as identifier, name, managingEntity, heartbeatPeriod, timeout, and maxCount. Optional additions do not invalidate R4 Subscriptions and are the compatibility-preserving way to add capability. They matter for R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but that is a data-loss mitigation issue rather than a base R4-to-R6 break.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.identifier` is `0..* Identifier` and `Subscription.name` is `0..1 string`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.managingEntity` is `0..1 Reference` to a bounded set of actor resources.
R6 StructureDefinition: `heartbeatPeriod`, `timeout`, and `maxCount` are optional numeric delivery-control fields.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use does not make optional additive content a forward compatibility concern. It only reminds implementers not to silently discard populated R6 fields when bridging back to R4.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: populated R6-only fields have no native R4 locations; there is no old-valid/new-invalid break because R4 instances simply omit them.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable as a less-breaking R6 base design, because optional additions already preserve R4-valid instances. Extensions can support R4 round-trip, but that is an implementation mitigation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-direction data-loss note, but disagree with elevating optional additions to a medium R4-to-R6 compatibility impact.

findings.title: R6 filterBy introduces mandatory child fields and a new comparator/modifier mutual-exclusion invariant

oldState.summary: R4 has no structured filterBy component; filtering is embedded in the required criteria string.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 does not validate search parameter structure inside `criteria` beyond the field being a string.

newState.summary: R6 filterBy repeats require filterParameter and value, may include comparator or modifier, and has invariant scr-1 forbidding both comparator and modifier in the same filter.

constraints.human: Subscription filters may only contain a modifier or a comparator

newState.narrativeMd: Each R6 filter row is structured and must conform to topic-allowed filter parameters, comparators, and modifiers.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The new invariant does not reject an untransformed R4 instance directly because R4 had no `filterBy`, but it constrains how R4 criteria may be transformed. A naive converter that puts both a comparator and modifier into one filter row will produce invalid R6. R6 filters also depend on SubscriptionTopic definitions, so syntactically valid rows can still be semantically invalid for a topic.

justification.inferredGoal: Make subscriber filters machine-validatable and disallow ambiguous comparator/modifier combinations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: `filterBy` is new optional R6 content, and its invariant does not directly reject an R4-valid instance.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The `scr-1` invariant is reasonable because a structured filter row with both comparator and modifier would be ambiguous. This finding is not itself a breaking R4-to-R6 base-design issue; the R4-breaking design choice is the removal of `criteria`, which is covered separately.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Backward-compatible alternative analysis is not applicable to the new optional `filterBy` constraint. A normative parser or mapping guide for R4 criteria would be useful migration support, but under the calibration rules that is tooling/guidance rather than a less-breaking base R6 design for this specific finding.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The compatibility burden belongs to criteria-to-topic migration; the new filter constraint itself is an R6 validation rule rather than a less-breaking base alternative question.

evidence.detail: R6 adds a local error-level invariant forbidding both comparator and modifier.
R6 filterParameter is mandatory.
R6 value is mandatory.
R6 comparator required value set contains eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le, sa, eb, ap.
R6 modifier required value set contains missing, exact, contains, not, text, in, not-in, below, above, type, identifier, of-type, code-text, text-advanced, iterate.

examples.examplesMd: A converter should represent comparator and modifier choices in separate valid patterns or reject unsupported criteria. For example, a single R6 `filterBy` row with both `comparator` and `modifier` violates `scr-1`.

findings.narrativeMd: R6's `filterBy` is not just a string decomposition of R4 criteria. It has mandatory child fields, required bindings for comparator/modifier, a local error-level invariant, and semantic dependence on the referenced SubscriptionTopic. This creates validation rules that R4 did not have for the criteria string itself.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4→R6: migrated filters can become invalid if required child fields are missing, comparator/modifier codes are outside the required value sets, or both comparator and modifier are populated. R6→R4: structured filters can often be serialized into a search string, but topic-defined events and resource scoping may not round-trip cleanly.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Use a real FHIR search parser rather than string splitting. Validate each candidate filter against the target SubscriptionTopic's `canFilterBy` rules and against `scr-1`. Keep fixtures for simple token filters, comparators, modifiers, multiple filters with AND semantics, and event filters with OR semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The constraint is a reasonable local validation rule in R6. The avoidable part is the lack of a native compatibility lane for old criteria strings, not the existence of the constraint itself.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 `filterBy` is new optional content with mandatory child fields and an error invariant forbidding both comparator and modifier in the same row. Since R4 has no `filterBy`, this constraint does not itself reject an R4-valid Subscription. It is important for converters that map R4 criteria into R6 filters, but the base compatibility break is the criteria-to-topic redesign covered separately.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition: `Subscription.filterBy` is `0..* BackboneElement`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `filterBy.filterParameter` and `filterBy.value` are both `1..1 string`.
R6 invariant `scr-1` is error-level: `Subscription filters may only contain a modifier or a comparator`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 3/trial-use warrants attention to criteria migration, but for this specific optional R6-only constraint it does not create a forward compatibility problem.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: none: the invariant applies only when R6 `filterBy` is populated; invalid migrated filters are a conversion-tooling problem tied to the separate criteria replacement.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Not applicable for this specific finding. Downgrading the invariant to a warning would make ambiguous R6 filters easier to create and would not preserve any R4-valid instance, because no R4 instance had `filterBy`.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing potential-hard-break framing for this isolated finding; it is useful migration guidance but not a separate base compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag are unchanged. R6 changes status from draft to active and standards-status from trial-use to normative, but that is not an instance-shape breaking change.

The retained local modifier element `Subscription.status` remains `isModifier=true` with the same modifier reason. No new local Subscription element other than inherited/base fields is marked as a modifier; inherited modifierExtension behavior is out of scope.
No local Subscription elements in the inspected R4 or R6 definitions add fixed values, pattern values, or default values.
No local Subscription elements add maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraints in the inspected definitions. New numeric delivery-control elements have primitive datatype limits only.
No local Subscription slicing definitions were found in either version's Subscription StructureDefinition.

There is no pre-existing R4 local Reference-valued Subscription element whose target list was narrowed. R6 adds `topic` canonical and `managingEntity` Reference targets; those R6-only representability effects are covered in findings.

Retained local elements such as `status`, `contact`, `end`, and `reason` remain summary elements. Summary behavior changes tied to removed/moved channel fields, especially `channel.header` to non-summary `parameter`, are covered in findings rather than listed as no-change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status/maturity increased in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 marks the StructureDefinition status as active and its standards-status extension as normative while retaining the same canonical identity and resource type. This does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The maturity change may influence governance and implementation priority, but it should not be treated as an instance conversion rule.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Contact and end retain cardinality, datatype, and summary status
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Subscription.contact` remains `0..* ContactPoint` and `Subscription.end` remains `0..1 instant`; both remain summary elements with materially similar definitions.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: These fields can generally be carried forward unchanged while surrounding topic/channel fields are transformed.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Existing R4 status codes are retained in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Although R6 adds `entered-in-error`, the R4 codes `requested`, `active`, `error`, and `off` are still present in the local R6 subscription-status CodeSystem.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 instances using old status codes do not need status-code remapping for R4→R6, but R6 consumers must handle the additional code.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Subscription.topic` is mandatory and `filterBy` semantics depend on `SubscriptionTopic.canFilterBy`, event triggers, resource definitions, and topic catalogs. Criteria migration cannot be finalized without analyzing SubscriptionTopic in depth.
R4 `Subscription.error` appears to move to the separate R6 `SubscriptionStatus.error` model, and notification lifecycle/state behavior should be assessed in the SubscriptionStatus report.
Channel type moved from primitive code to Coding and the value set now composes an external terminology.hl7.org CodeSystem. Confirm exact code set and system/version before automated conversion.
R6 payload content codes determine privacy- and delivery-relevant behavior that R4 could not express directly.
Any inherited base-definition, extension, or common-element changes should be handled by the base-artifact reports, not duplicated in this Subscription report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 Subscription diff, ballot change note, or migration guide was available in the local package directories. The report therefore infers migration intent from computable definitions and nearby artifacts.
